report: Shadow re-review of PR #1913 (issue #1905). Documentation-only diff: one rewritten embedded-jq gotcha bullet in CLAUDE.md plus one new .changeset/issue-1905-embedded-jq-lint-surfaces.md; no executable code. Diff profile: docs/config-only, no new types, no test files. Phase 0.4 resolved 6 acceptance criteria from issue #1905; all six code-verifiable criteria are satisfied by the diff. Both load-bearing factual claims in the rewritten bullet were verified independently against the tree: (1) .github/workflows/ci.yml (lines 413-420) contains the raven-actions/actionlint@v2 step running shellcheck over workflow run: blocks with SHELLCHECK_OPTS excluding only SC2034, so the apostrophe-terminated-string checks (SC1073/SC1011/SC1112) fire in inline jq inside a workflow — the old 'lint never reaches the workflow YAMLs' claim is correctly retired; (2) lib/fetch-pr-context.sh (lines 573-589) holds the live reduce ($lines[0:30][]) as $l (...) using the bind-before-test pattern ($l | test(...), .fence as $f), exactly the fix the new test() trap clause names. The bullet retains the string-op-aborts-whole-filter warning and its (.x | strings) guard. No documented_falsehood introduced; the diff corrects a prior false claim rather than adding one. Phase 2 checklist verification: no failing claims. Phase 3 roster: 4 always-on agents dispatched and all returned; type-design-analyzer and pr-test-analyzer gated out (has_new_types false; no test file and docs/config-only diff). One Suggestion-level finding from the final-pass reviewer (an asserted-but-unpinned behavioral claim about actionlint coverage), below any REJECT threshold and not demotable to a defect here. Verdict: APPROVE.

phase3_findings.description: The claim that actionlint's bundled shellcheck catches an apostrophe-terminated single-quoted jq string in a workflow run: block is an empirical behavioral claim asserted without an in-repo pin or worked example. It is technically plausible and consistent with the pre-existing ci.yml:413 comment, so low risk, but a reader could over-rely on it as guaranteed coverage if a future config disabled run:-block shellcheck. Optional hardening only.
